l0.speaker: narrator
l0.text: Friday. The main quad has disappeared under folding tables, banners, and free stickers. Every club on campus is shouting at once.

l1.speaker: quack
l1.text: The club fair! Everyone here wants you to join something. Take the free stuff. Commit to nothing. Well. Commit to a little.

l2.speaker: narrator
l2.text: The gardening club table is covered in potted herbs. Behind it, someone in an oversized cardigan is handing out tea in paper cups.

l3.speaker: python
l3.text: {player}! You found us. Here, it's mint. We grew it ourselves.

l4.speaker: python
l4.text: The gardening club meets Saturday and Sunday mornings in the greenhouse. Nobody minds if you just come to sit with the plants.

l5.speaker: python
l5.text: And on weeknights I work the tutoring center shift in Turing Hall. I bring tea and stay late. If you're stuck on anything, come find me there.

l6.speaker: narrator
l6.text: Two tables down, the student council booth is perfectly squared to the edge of the lawn. Every flyer on it is lined up to the millimeter.

l7.speaker: java
l7.text: Ah. {player}. Good afternoon. Please, take a schedule. It's laminated.

l8.speaker: java
l8.text: Council office hours are Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings in the council room in Oracle Hall. I am always there early. Always.

l9.speaker: java
l9.text: I also chair the coffee appreciation society, Monday to Thursday mornings at Café Cache. Attendance is optional. It is noticed, but optional.

l10.speaker: narrator
l10.text: At the end of the row is a table with a cardboard sign: GAME DEV CLUB. Under it, in smaller handwriting: GO AWAY (we are recruiting).

l11.speaker: narrator
l11.text: Nobody is sitting at it. Ciel is leaning against the tree next to it, typing on a keyboard balanced on one arm.

l12.speaker: cpp
l12.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm not in the club. There is no club. It's not official.

l13.speaker: cpp
l13.text: I'm in the game dev club room in the Student Union on Friday, Saturday and Sunday mornings. Coincidentally. Whenever I'm there.

l14.speaker: cpp
l14.text: Monday to Thursday nights I'm in Hopper Lab running benchmarks. There's a spare seat. It's not for you. It's just spare.

l15.speaker: narrator
l15.text: By the Computer Science department tent, Jay is sorting sign-up sheets into color-coded folders, glasses pushed up, tablet in hand.

l16.speaker: javascript
l16.text: Good afternoon, {player}. Your lanyard is on backwards. Please fix that before we continue.

l17.speaker: javascript
l17.text: TA office hours are weekdays during the day, in the TA office in Turing Hall. Bring your code and your exact error message. "It doesn't work" is not an error message.

l18.speaker: narrator
l18.text: Next to the tent, a bright yellow banner is zip-tied to a lamppost. There's nobody at its table, just a stack of flyers held down by a slice of cold pizza.

l19.speaker: narrator
l19.text: HACKATHON NIGHTS!!! Saturday + Sunday nights, Student Union hackathon hall. Free pizza. Bring friends. Bring ANYONE. Signed: J.

l20.speaker: javascript
l20.text: That table is not affiliated with the department. I don't go to those. I'm asleep by ten.

l21.speaker: javascript
l21.text: ...I think. There's a sticker on my tablet I don't remember buying.

l22.speaker: quack
l22.text: Okay, {player}, schedule talk. Remember: every day has two slots, Day and Night. A lesson uses up one of them, so pick who you spend it with.

l23.speaker: quack
l23.text: Weekdays have classes during the day. Weekends are wide open, day and night. And everyone you just met has the same places they go every week.

l24.speaker: quack
l24.text: It's all on your calendar, the button next to Menu. If you can't find someone, check it. If they're not on it, they're probably asleep.

l25.speaker: quack
l25.text: Although Jay has office hours every weekday, and the hackathon guy runs all weekend nights... When does anyone around here sleep? It's like Jay has two completely different schedules.

l26.speaker: quack
l26.text: Anyway! Lesson 2, Comments, is open now. Anyone here can teach it, but there's only time for one of them before tonight. You can do it with the others later.

pick.speaker: quack
pick.text: So? Who are you going to ask?

choices.text: President Duke. The schedule was laminated.
Ciel. The spare seat sounded like a dare.
Jay. I'll bring my exact error message.

pick_python.speaker: quack
pick_python.text: Safe pick. Monty would teach a rock to code if it sat still long enough.

pick_java.speaker: quack
pick_java.text: Bold. Bring a pen. There will be forms.

pick_cpp.speaker: quack
pick_cpp.text: Oh no. Okay. If Ciel insults your code, that means it was worth insulting.

pick_javascript.speaker: quack
pick_javascript.text: Good choice. Fix your lanyard first.
